    8	/**
    9	 * The per-resource floor a planet must keep after a spend, so one purchase cannot starve the next.
   10	 *
   11	 * A build that consumes the last metal stops the next save, the next commitment and the next research
   12	 * step, so a player reserves first: keep a small fraction of what the planet holds and let the
   13	 * production that arrives while saving refill it (SP5). The floor is the buffer reduced by that
   14	 * production, and it is never negative. Each resource's floor guards that resource alone, so a planet
   15	 * saving deuterium for a drive is not frozen out of spending its surplus metal and crystal: a purchase
   16	 * that spends no deuterium must keep no deuterium floor. The buffer, the economy horizon and the
   17	 * research horizon are the published defaults the corpus documents; none of them names a game object,
   18	 * so nothing here encodes the host's universe.
   19	 */
   20	class ReserveFloor
   21	{
   22	    /** Keep this fraction of what the planet holds per resource (SP5, `keep_resources_buffer`). */
   23	    public const BUFFER = 0.10;
   24	
   25	    /** How many hours of production may refill the floor for an economy spend (SP5). */
   26	    public const ECONOMY_HOURS = 4.0;
   27	
   28	    /** How many hours of production may refill the floor for a research spend (SP5). */
   29	    public const RESEARCH_HOURS = 6.0;
   30	
   31	    /**
   32	     * The floor that must survive a purchase, per resource, at this planet.
   33	     *
   34	     * The buffer is a fraction of the balance, never of the storage capacity. A fresh planet holding
   35	     * 529 metal with room for 10,000 has almost nothing to protect, and a reserve charged on capacity
   36	     * refuses every purchase it could ever make -- including the mine that earns the reserve back --
   37	     * so the account stands still for good. Capping the buffer by the balance keeps the reserve real
   38	     * for a rich planet and harmless for a poor one.
   39	     *
   40	     * @param float $savingHours how long the account is willing to wait for production to refill
   41	     */
   42	    public function floor(PlanetService $planet, float $savingHours): Resources
   43	    {
   44	        $held = $planet->getResources();
   45	
   46	        // An account whose public score has not moved for hours is saving for nothing: the reserve is
   47	        // released so the queue spends what is held, which is what a player does on noticing a stall.
   48	        if (app(StalledGrowthDetector::class)->stalled((int) $planet->getPlayer()?->getId())) {
   49	            return new Resources(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
   50	        }
   51	
   52	        return new Resources(
   53	            $this->perResource($held->metal->get(), $planet->getMetalProductionPerHour(), $savingHours),
   54	            $this->perResource($held->crystal->get(), $planet->getCrystalProductionPerHour(), $savingHours),
   55	            $this->perResource($held->deuterium->get(), $planet->getDeuteriumProductionPerHour(), $savingHours),
   56	        );
   57	    }
   58	
   59	    private function perResource(float $held, float $productionPerHour, float $savingHours): float
   60	    {
   61	        return max(0.0, $held * self::BUFFER - $productionPerHour * $savingHours);
   62	    }
   63	}

For the homeworld with mines at similar levels, all are expensive. But colonies! The account has 7 planets; each has its own build slot; the homeworld would still progress. So (B) can't explain a total absence... unless all planets have at least one cheap mine (colonies are young; the homeworld too?). Hmm: at 1000x, does the *cheapest* paying mine stay cheap? The account spends on the cheapest mining upgrade each login (the fastest payback) → hmm, `production()` sorts by payback hours, and `firstQueueable` takes the first affordable. So the account builds the mine with the best payback (usually the lowest level mine) → mines get *levelled* by payback, keeping all three mines at similar payback — i.e. metal mine level ~5 above crystal (since payback normalizes), but all mines would be at high levels... Buildings: 317 orders in 30 min for 100 accounts with 7 planets each = 700 planets → 317 orders / 700 planets = 0.45 per planet per 30 min. So each planet builds once per hour. Over a day: 24 builds. Over several days: 50-100 builds per planet. With ~30 mine levels + storages + stations, plausible that mines are at level 25-35 and the station project is reachable.

Hmm, so what if the gate IS open and station candidates ARE offered and the planet builds robot_factory → 10, comp tech → 10, and then nano factory → 1... and the live evidence says the sim's 2h doesn't produce it. Hmm, but that would mean the cohort should already have it — unless all this just happened after the previous change? The previous check ran the sim immediately after the previous change landed, so the sim only gave 2 hours for a climb that requires several steps (robot 10, comp 10, note comp 10 also needs research lab 10!). Hmm! computer_technology 10 requires research_lab 10 (host: computer tech requirements = espionage tech? let me check ResearchObjects). And research_lab 10 requires robot_factory 10? Let's check.

Also research time for computer tech 10 could be hours at research speed 1. So a 2h sim can't complete the climb from scratch. So my fix must make at least one account cross the finish line *quickly*, ideally within the 2h sim, or be already close on the live cohort (live accounts continue in real time, and the live proof is re-run periodically — maybe the live proof they run later will show it).

Hmm! Important: if the sim runs first and passes, then the live steps are judged on the copy — a passing sim means proof PASS. So the sim is the target: 2h on 30 accounts. So my change must yield a nano factory within 2h of simulated play starting from the current cohort DB. Since the cohort state is unknown to me, I must make the path *fast* for a mature account: e.g., station steps allowed on planets that can afford them, without the "mines outgrown" gate blocking, and quickly (the account has money at 1000x, so it can queue robot_factory 10 immediately, then comp tech, then nano).

Wait, but the sim's accounts are the first 30. Live evidence accounts already hold alliance_depot and missile_silo (deep). So they're mature.

So the key question remains: what blocks it now? Options: (A) surplus pass, (B) mine gate, (C) the nano candidate being outranked by the chain (war hull) — no, station comes first, (D) the doctrine pass, (E) cost/refusal.

Next: "price plus reserve" → `$planet->hasResources($this->withReserve(...))` — reserve floor 4h production, but capped by `held*0.1 - production*4h` → at 1000x, production*4h >> held*0.1 typically, so floor = 0. Hmm, what about the *research* gate for computer_technology 10: `queueableResearch` requires `!retrieveQueue($planet)->isQueueFull()` and `objectRequirementsMetWithQueue` and `hasResources(price + reserve)`. Fine.

What about the lab slot competition: on each login, the lab is filled once. The research candidates come from the doctrine's research path (which includes astrophysics to 7 and plasma 8 — deep, expensive). Hmm, doctrine 'research' pass candidate is used if the lab slot isn't taken by an earlier pass's research candidate. The passes are ordered; 'routine' is where the chain's research lives, and 'doctrine' comes earlier! So the doctrine's research step (e.g. plasma_technology 8 or astrophysics 7) is offered before the chain's computer_technology 10... but doctrine researchStep returns only the FIRST unmet step, and if that step isn't queueable (price/lab), withStep's firstQueueable returns null for the lab slot, and the routine pass's research candidates then get their chance. Hmm OK. I think I need to actually *look* at the live-ish state. Here's an idea: the harness's `sim` command uses `ai:sim` from the module scripts. Right — the tests avoid the surplus pass. So live, with 1000x and the same stores, storage full is very plausible... Actually hmm: capacity 10.5 billion at level 20 — reaching that requires accumulating 10.5B metal, which at 1000x production with deep mines is possible (mines 30 → 30*30*1.1^30*1000 ≈ 30*30*17*1000 = 15M/h, so 10.5B takes 700h). Hmm, that's 30 days. So metal storage might not be full. But crystal store level 14 → 10000*2^14 = 164M crystal; crystal production maybe 5M/h → 33h to fill. Plausible to be full!

So the surplus pass is plausibly firing often. Hmm, but hold on: would a full warehouse survive? That's a strong, structural deadlock: "a planet at capacity spends its surplus on the fastest mine every login".

Wait, but the 'storage' pass comes even before 'surplus': storage offers a bigger warehouse when the fill time is less than the absence. If the fill time is less than absence → build a storage; if the storage is already full (time to fill = 0) → storage() skips (hours <= 0) → surplus handles it. So at capacity, storage pass is empty, surplus fires.

So a planet that is at capacity spends on a mine forever; the station project (later pass) never fires; the nano factory is never built. THAT would explain the live failure, and it also explains why the previous fix (stationPending with the mines gate) works in tests (which never plant a full warehouse) but not live.

But wait: if storage is full and the surplus pass keeps buying mines, does the mine keep being affordable? Yes.

Hmm, is this specific to 1000x? At speed 1 the fill times are long, and the storage pass builds storages to prevent overflow, so capacity is rarely reached. At 1000x, the storage pass's condition `buildHours < absence` fails (build times are not speed-scaled) → storages stop growing → the planet sits at capacity → surplus forever.

So the fix: give the station project its turn ahead of the surplus spend, or exclude the station goal from the surplus pre-emption. Per style: "where a ratio and a cap conflict at the extreme, the cap wins" — not relevant.

Which is the smallest, principled change? The comment in the code for the surplus pass says: "E7: a full warehouse is a spend signal — the surplus is a permanent loss, so the best mine is offered with no payback horizon and the planner spends the surplus rather than discarding it." The station project is also a spend of the surplus — arguably better: it's a goal the account named. A human with a full warehouse and an affordable station buys the station.

So: in the routine pass, put the station project ahead of the surplus pass? Can't — the passes are separate top-level keys; I'd reorder 'surplus' after 'routine'? But that reordering doesn't by itself give the station project priority over surplus: if 'routine' comes before 'surplus', the routine pass's own candidates are tried — the first candidate is energy, then stationPending (if the gate says so), then chain, then storageForPrice, then paying mines. So with full storage, the routine would offer the station (if allowed) → the planet builds the station. And the surplus (INF-horizon mines) still runs for planets whose routine came up empty. That's a coherent, small change: move 'surplus' after 'routine'. Hmm, but 'ambition' is after; fine.

Hmm, is there a test that asserts the surplus pass ordering? Let's search for spendSurplus in tests.

Confirms: since 17 Sep, a field-full planet + full warehouse → the surplus pass routes to a research dump (armor tech etc.). This has been live and it's why the planets "cannot build". So the live cohort's planets are field-full and dumping surplus into research — that mechanism exists live (matches live evidence "research 70 orders" and "QueueResearch Completed 86").

Hmm, but the invariant says nano factory etc. unheld. Since field-full planets can't build anything field-consuming — including the nano factory — the nano can only be built on a planet with a free field. Field-full planets can't be fixed (terraformer refused). So on the live cohort, how many planets have a free field? A new colony always starts with a free field; a colony quickly fills.

Hmm wait, but that suggests the real fix is to make the terraformer reachable — it's the object that un-blocks everything (nano is 1 field). But the host refuses the terraformer when full.

Let me examine the host more carefully: is the terraformer really refused by the host when the planet is full? BuildingQueueService::start(): `if ($building->consumesPlanetField) { if ($currentBuildingCount >= $maxFields) throw ... }`. The terraformer's consumesPlanetField is true (default). So yes, refused. Hmm, but maybe the *host* has a special case in the front-end/normal OGame logic: the terraformer increases fields, so the check should compare count+1 > max+5*levels... The message says "Upgrade your Terraformer or use a planet field item" for a planet → implying that the terraformer CAN be built even when full (otherwise the message is nonsense). So the host's check is arguably a bug (bug for the host repo, not my task). We can't change the host. Hmm, but the *rules* say never restate a host rule... but if the host refuses, our queue can't do it.

So the terraformer is unreachable once field-full, and nano along with it (since nano consumes a field). To get the nano factory held live, some planet must build it while a field is free.

Given the accounts are 3.5 days old at 1000x with field-full planets, and there's no free-field planet... unless the newest colony has a free field for a short while. A new colony starts with mines 0 and 200 fields free — the colony builds mines up. So a fresh colony has free fields for a while (levels). At 1000x the account colonises (Colonisation missions 2 in 30 min). So fresh colonies exist with free fields. On a fresh colony, `minesOutgrownStations` false (mines cheap) → no station project → mines until fields fill up (~40 levels later... 100+ builds). At 0.45 builds/planet/30min → hmm, per planet ~1 build/hour → 100 builds = 4+ days. So a fresh colony won't hit the station project before filling? It has 200 fields: 3 mines × 40 levels = 120 + solar 40 = 160 + stores 60 = 220 → full at about the same time as the station gate opens (mines ~30-45). Hmm! So the race is: by the time the mines are expensive enough to trigger the station project, the fields are (nearly) full → the station project's steps are refused by 'no free field'. Wow, that's a plausible deadlock: the two gates cross.

So: the live cohort's planets are field-full (as the refusals show), and the station project's gate (mines outgrown) opens only when the mines are deep — which is exactly when the fields run out. So nano is never buildable.

Hmm, so is the fix "the station project should be scheduled before the fields run out"? That's "keep a field free for the terraformer". A human player at 1000x who knows the game would indeed build the terraformer proactively... but the plan's own gate refuses it when full.

Hmm, hold on. Let me reconsider whether nano/terraformer really need a free field: `consumesPlanetField` — the terraformer adds 5 fields per level *plus* consumes 1, so net +4. If the planet is full and the terraformer could be built, the account would be fine. The host's own message literally tells the player to upgrade the terraformer. Maybe the host's `start()` check is buggy but the *front-end* `AbstractBuildingsController` computes `fields_exceeded` and maybe still allows the request, and the controller also calls BuildingQueueService::start() which throws... So the terraformer is truly blocked on a full planet. Ugh.

Let me test this in a Situation: plant a field-full planet (fields exhausted) with robot 10 + comp 10 + stock; then see whether the session queues nano_factory. If the diagnosis says 'no free field' for the station steps, that confirms the field deadlock. And the fix would then be: the building planner must schedule the station project (or at least the terraformer) *before* the planet is full — i.e., treat "fields nearly exhausted" as a spend signal that puts the terraformer/station project ahead of routine mining. Hmm! But the terraformer requires nano_factory 1 — so on a nearly-full planet the account must first build nano, then terraformer before the last field is used. Both need one field. Fields are consumed as buildings complete... A practical rule: when the free fields are nearly exhausted (say, the planet has no room for the next mine), the station project (nano factory → terraformer) is the step, ahead of mining — because mining cannot continue afterwards anyway.

But in the check I might not reproduce "field-full" from the live cohort in the sim: after my change, on a live planet with N free fields, the account would build nano (1 field) then terraformer (+4 net) and then keep mining. For planets with ZERO free fields, nothing can be done (host rule). So the fix works only if some planets still have ≥2 free fields. Live refusals show some planets have none. Hmm, but with 100 accounts and 700 planets, surely some have free fields.

Hmm, but the current code's gate for the station project requires mines-outgrown; on a planet with a free field and cheap mines (a young colony) the gate is false → mining. So the fix: when the planet's fields are nearly full (no free field *for the next step*), the station project must take priority — because it's the only way to keep growing. That's a specific, evidence-backed rule. And "nearly full" I'd define as: the planet has no free fields, or the next thing the account wants cannot fit... Hmm.

Hmm, hmm. Time check: I've spent a lot of reads. I must edit soon. Let me settle on the most defensible change with the evidence I have, and design the plan's numbers into YAML.

Wait — before that, let me reconsider the simplest explanation I might be missing: does the inventory of "fields full" explain no *nano* across all accounts? The live cohort is 100 accounts... the invariant lists only nano as the first missing. So yes: no account has nano. If fields were the cause on most planets, we'd still expect a few planets with room. Unless every planet that has room is a young colony where the station gate is false.

So the two gates interlock exactly as I described: fields fill by the time mines are expensive. That's a strong, coherent story: the station project's trigger (mines outgrown) fires too late — after the planet can no longer build.

Now, what's the *smallest, principled* fix? A human rule: "keep a field free for the terraformer" — the station project should get its turn while the planet still has the room to build it. Implement in the gate `minesOutgrownStations` (rename? keep name) — extend the condition: the station project also has its turn when the planet can no longer fit its next mine (fields nearly exhausted)... Hmm, but "fields exhausted" means even the nano factory can't fit, so the trigger must be *proactive*: the station project should pre-empt the mine when the number of free fields is small (e.g. the remaining free fields are fewer than the levels the mines still have room to grow?). A simple, human rule: when the planet's free fields will run out before the mines stop repaying... hmm, too clever.

Simpler and defensible: the station project takes the planet's build slot when the planet's fields are nearly used up — defined as free fields ≤ the number of levels the next mine needs before the fields run out? Hmm. Let me define: "free fields" = max - count. If free <= 0, nothing to do (host refuses all field-consuming). If free is small (say ≤ the fields the account's remaining mine ladder would need... unknown), the account should spend its remaining fields on the station range (nano+terraformer = 2 fields: nano 1, terraformer 1 → then terraformer adds 5/level). Hmm, so the rule: "when the free fields are not enough for both the next mine and the station the host offers, the station goes first" — i.e., if free fields < 1( mine) + 2 (nano+terraformer)... Hmm.

Hmm, but does a *human* do that? At 1000x yes-ish. But hmm — the plan already has a "storage full" spend signal; fields are the analogue: "fields full is a station signal".

Alternatively — a much simpler fix, and maybe the actual intended one: the *field* gate should not block the station project's steps from *falling through*, and... no, that doesn't create nano.

Let me look at the problem from the "what did the owner's note say" angle: "Root causes fixed in 7a03102 and the commit after: stations are chain goals (robotics 10 -> nano -> terraformer), moons keep their fields for the lunar base, an energy-priced technology raises the plant (graviton -> deathstar)." — "moons keep their fields for the lunar base" implies the plan *reserves* fields for key objects on moons. So there IS an existing notion of reserving fields. Let's grep for that ("keep their fields", field reservation) in the module.

reasoning_content:
"moons keep their fields for the lunar base" — the note references the FixedX commit; the implementation is in FacilityChain (moon block: the chain includes the lunar base/phalanx and the naked-wall rule skips moons). "Moons keep their fields for the lunar base" = the wall prerequisites are not applied on moons (so the lunar base gets the field). OK.

Given the time, let me now decide. I'll go with the field-capacity interlock, because:
- The live refusal list *proves* planets are field-full (4 in 30 min).
- The task notes mention "moons keep their fields for the lunar base" — fields are a known competing resource in this problem space.
- A field-full planet can never build the nano factory nor the terraformer, whatever the mines-outgrown gate says.

But hmm, wait. Is it really true that a deep planet reaches the station gate only after the fields are full? Let's quantify: fields 200. Station gate needs the cheapest paying mine > cheapest unheld station (< 1.6M-ish). A mine's price passes 1.6M at metal_mine level ~21 (60*1.5^20 = 199k... let me compute properly: 60*1.5^(n-1). n=20: 60*1.5^19=60*2216=133k; n=25: 60*1.5^24=60*16834=1.01M; n=27: 60*1.5^26=60*37876=2.27M). So the metal mine passes 1.6M at level ~26. Crystal mine: 48*1.6^(n-1): n=20 → 48*1.6^19 = 48*7655=367k; n=23: 48*1.6^22 = 48*3e4=1.4M → ~level 23. Deut synth: 225*1.5^(n-1): n=20: 225*1.5^19=225*2216=498k; n=25: 225*16834=3.8M → ~level 22.

Fields used at those levels: 26+23+22 = 71 fields — way below 200! Plus solar plant (level ~40?): but the solar plant's energy needs a level similar to the mines... at 1000x the energy demand is the same ratios: solar plant level ≈ 1.5x mines? Hmm, solar plant level n produces 20*1.1^n... The solar plant level for mines at 26 would be around 30. Actually the energy consumption of a mine is 10*1.1^level... The plant level needed is roughly the mine level + a few. So ~80 fields total including storage. So a planet at mines 26 has used maybe 90 fields — not full!

So fields are NOT the reason the station project can't run on a mature planet. Hmm! But then why 4 field refusals live? Because at 1000x the planets are deep: mines at 40+ → 3*40=120 + solar 45 = 165 + stores 60 = 225 > 200. So they overshoot at high levels; the field-full state is what *stops* further growth (that's why the accounts are stalled — "STALLED" aspect).

OK so, the live cohort's planets: many at/over the field cap. Those planets can't build anything field-consuming. Hmm, and here's the thing: the station gate needs the mines to be expensive — which they are on THOSE planets. So the gate is TRUE on the field-full planets, the station project is offered, but its steps are refused ('no free field') → falls through to research. Hence no nano factory anywhere. And on planets with free fields the mines are cheaper → gate false.

Wait, but that's not inevitable: the field-full planets had free fields when the mines were ~level 26 (the gate's threshold) — at that point the gate was true (mines 26 > 1.6M? yes) and the fields had room → the station project should have fired then! Unless the gate's threshold is much higher: `cheapestStationPrice` — the cheapest station the planet does NOT hold. If the account hasn't built the space_dock (cheap: 200 metal/50 deut/50 energy → sum 300), the gate compares against 300! Then the gate requires the cheapest paying mine > 300 → true from very early (mines > level 12) → the station project fires early (space_dock), builds it → then the next cheapest unheld station (missile_silo 41k? or research_lab?)... So the gate would fire early and build the stations in price order, eventually reaching nano (needs robot 10/comp 10). Hmm! So the station project should fire EARLY on live, not late. Then robot_factory 10, comp 10, nano... Hmm, unless the cheapest station is unaffordable...

Argh. I need the live state. Let me try to get it from the sim tool? No bash.

Hmm, what about the `why` read: "published: build, queue_units, spy, throttle_mine; NOT published: research, colonize". "research" NOT published means the research capability is off — i.e., no research candidate? That's interesting: player 35 has 7 planets, plenty of resources... Hmm, "NOT published: research" might mean the research queue is unavailable (e.g. no lab or lab busy).

I think I've been reading too long. Time to make a decision and edit.

DECISION: I'll go with the "surplus pass pre-empts the station project" theory? Or the field theory? Hmm.

Let me get one more piece of evidence cheaply: the live host orders say "buildings 317, research 70" in 30 min. If the field-full planets couldn't build, the building orders would be lower... 317 buildings/30min is high. Hmm, and if full planets dumped into research, research would dominate.

Also "QueueBuilding: nothing_queueable 1" and "Not enough fields 4" — so the building lane is mostly working.

Hmm, what about "sessions chose: Build 2%"? In the *pulse* the session's chosen action includes Build rarely. But the hosts' 317 building orders come from the planners' steps (ECON-001), not the session choice.

OK, let me try yet another approach to get ground truth: the check tool runs the proof (which includes the sim). Its output will show me the sim verdict — including maybe the refusals/why of the accounts. If my change is wrong, the output might still be informative (e.g., the invariant line names a different object, or the sim's refusals list). But each check costs. I have a handful. Fine: I'll make a change aimed at the most likely cause, write a Situation test as the task requires, and check once to learn.

Now: which change has the best chance? Let me think about what a "correct" fix looks like that a human would do and that unblocks nano *soon* (within 2 sim hours) from an unknown-but-mature state:

The most robust fix: **make the station project a chain goal that outranks the routine mine when the station is affordable and the planet's fields are nearly exhausted OR the mines are outgrown** — hmm, too many knobs.

Alternative robust fix: make the *station* steps part of the ordinary chain ambition order, i.e. `FacilityChain::ambitions()` currently sorts stations by price but puts the war hull first (`$warHull`). The ambition's prerequisites govern the chain: the chain serves ONE ambition — the war hull if pending. So the station's prerequisites (robot 10, comp 10) never become chain steps. The previous attempt added a separate stationPending list gated on mines-outgrown. A cleaner fix: include the station goals in the "ambition" ordering ahead of the war hull when the station is affordable... Hmm.

Hmm, let me think about what's cheapest and most likely to make an account reach nano within 2 hours:
1. The account needs robot_factory 10 (price 205k/61k/102k — cheap), computer tech 10 (research: 10 levels... at 1000x research costs? research_speed maybe 1 → times could be long: computer tech level 10 costs ~ 0+... research time maybe hours. Hmm, computer_technology requires espionage_technology 2 and... let me check the host's research requirements for computer technology: it might require nothing. And each level's time grows; level 10 could take a while at research speed 1 (the universe has research_speed? maybe 1000 too?). If research speed is 1, computer tech 10 might take hours — so a 2h sim can't do it from 0. But live accounts likely already have computer tech 10? (the doctrine path goes to computer_technology 2 only; the fleet-slot ceiling adds more if slot-bound — most accounts have 11 free slots).

So the nano climb needs comp 10 — probably a multi-hour climb → 2h sim can't show it unless something is already there.

Hmm, that makes the whole "sim 2h" target nearly impossible for the nano factory unless the research is fast or accounts are already close. Unless... the invariants are evaluated on the sim copy at SIM_NOW but the *cohort history* counts: the invariant just checks DB rows (planets/users_tech) — a nano built 10 minutes into the sim counts. Fine.

OK — hmm, let me reconsider: maybe the answer is much dumber and closer to the previous failure. What if the whole thing hinges on `FacilityChain::pending()` — which the routine pass calls — and the previous attempt's `stationPending` is only reached when `minesOutgrownStations`, and the notes' claim "stations are chain goals" means the *chain* (pending) should include stations as ambitions — which it does (`$stations` merged into `$objects` in `ambitions()`). But `nextAmbition` only returns the *first* ambition with unmet prerequisites — with the war hull forced first (`$warHull`). So stations are never the ambition's top pick... and the "ambition" economy pass (6x vault) is the fallback. So the chain's station ambition rarely fires.

Which means: THE route to nano is `stationPending` (gated) or `EconomyUpgrades::ambitions` (6x price vault, level<3, and only for objects whose requirements are MET — so nano requires robot 10/comp 10 met, which nothing else delivers!). Circular: ambitions() skips objects with unmet requirements (`ObjectService::objectRequirementsMet`), and the chain skips stations because the war hull is first... So the ONLY source of robot_factory 10 / computer_technology 10 is `stationPending`.

So the gating on minesOutgrownStations is the single point of failure. On the live cohort it apparently almost never fires (per the invariant). Why? Two possibilities: (i) at least one paying mine candidate is always cheaper than the cheapest unheld station (e.g. the cheapest unheld station is the terraformer 150k or nano 1.6M, and the *deuterium synthesizer*'s next level is cheap because deut is expensive on energy... hmm no, deut synth at 20 = 498k < 1.6M → gate false while deut synth is at level ≤ 25! And deut synth levels are typically *behind* metal/crystal by many levels (bad payback!). ### FacilityChain::stationFieldBudget(PlanetService $planet): int

```php
/**
 * The fields this planet still needs for the stations only a planet can hold, levels included.
 *
 * A planet's fields are what every station and every mine competes for, and the last of them decide
 * whether the account can ever hold the objects that are gated behind a station -- which is how a
 * cohort ends up with no nanite factory anywhere: the mines spend the final fields, and the one object
 * that adds fields (behind the nanite factory) needs a field of its own to be built at all. A player
 * keeps the fields the station project still needs for exactly that reason, so the plan has one place
 * that says how many those are. Nothing is named: the goals are the host's station catalogue and the
 * levels are the host's own recursive requirement graph.
 *
 * Zero when the planet owes nothing to the station project -- every station it can hold stands -- so a
 * settled planet keeps mining as before, and zero on a moon, whose own two stations the moon block
 * already decides (RV-008/RV-009).
 */
public function stationFieldBudget(PlanetService $planet): int
{
    if ($planet->getPlanetType() === PlanetType::Moon) {
        return 0;
    }

    $budget = 0;

    foreach (ObjectService::getStationObjects() as $station) {
        if (!ObjectService::objectValidPlanetType($station->machine_name, $planet)) {
            continue;
        }

        if ($planet->getObjectLevel($station->machine_name) < 1 && $station->consumesPlanetField) {
            $budget++;   // hmm: the station itself
        }

        foreach (ObjectService::getRecursiveRequirements($station->machine_name) as $machineName => $level) {
            $object = ObjectService::getObjectByMachineName($machineName);
            if (!$object->consumesPlanetField) continue;   // research has no field
            $missing = $level - $this->currentLevel($planet, $machineName);
            if ($missing > 0) $budget += $missing;
        }
    }

    return $budget;
}
```

public function stationFieldBudget(PlanetService $planet): int
{
    if ($planet->getPlanetType() === PlanetType::Moon) return 0;

    $needed = [];   // machine name => the level the station project must reach
    foreach (ObjectService::getStationObjects() as $station) {
        if (!ObjectService::objectValidPlanetType($station->machine_name, $planet)) continue;
        $needed[$station->machine_name] = max($needed[$station->machine_name] ?? 0, 1);
        foreach (ObjectService::getRecursiveRequirements($station->machine_name) as $name => $level) {
            $needed[$name] = max($needed[$name] ?? 0, $level);
        }
    }

    $budget = 0;
    foreach ($needed as $name => $level) {
        $object = ObjectService::getObjectByMachineName($name);
        if (!$object->consumesPlanetField) continue;   // a technology is built in the lab, not on a field
        $budget += max(0, $level - $this->currentLevel($planet, $name));
    }

    return $budget;
}
